name: Driver's Road West
tagline: Pegasis drives Daikoku, the Turnpike and a one-way car from Tokyo to Kyoto via Suzuka, then drifts at Rusutsu, while Aoki gets a full anime day in Tokyo, Kawasaki, the Sabbat towns and a final Tokyo goods day.
summary: Three Tokyo nights with a full anime day, Girls Band Cry in Kawasaki and a weekday Daikoku night. One Times car from Haneda (Jan 21) to Kyoto (Jan 23) carries the bags over the Hakone Turnpike, past Fuji and Suzuka, so no luggage on trains. Kyoto is the only Kansai base (3 nights) for Nara's hill fire, the Sabbat towns and Osaka. A second car in Hokkaido gives the Rusutsu drift course, 2.5 ski days, Asahiyama and Sapporo. You fly back to Tokyo on Feb 1, which is cheaper for both return flights and adds a last Tokyo goods day.

who.pegasis: In: Daikoku (he drives, no guide), Hakone Turnpike, Taikanzan, Otome Pass, Gotemba outlets, Suzuka EV kart, Rusutsu (he drives), Niseko, Asahiyama, Daruma, Garaku, Moiwa, Nakano, Radio Kaikan, SHELTER live, Maidreamin, Ikebukuro, Nara fire, Isetan half-price, City Hall view, Golden Gai, airport bus. Out: Onuma (4 h each way from Niseko, not worth it); the Toyota part of the Tokaido road plan (Nagoya is not on this route). He joins Aoki's Fuji museum as the fair trade for the Turnpike.
who.aoki: In: Suga stairs, Akihabara, maid cafés (Tokyo, Osaka, Sapporo), Nakano, Shimokitazawa and SHELTER, Girls Band Cry Kawasaki + Yako + Hachiko, Yokohama Chinatown and Cup Noodles, Daikoku, Tatsumi/Umihotaru, Hakone Eva lake, Fuji museum, Lake Kawaguchi, Yuru Camp Motosu, Suzuka, Nara, Fushimi Inari at dawn, Kinkakuji, Sabbat (Kyoto, Kobe, Osaka), Namba food, Den Den Town, Liberty Walk, Rusutsu, Niseko beginner day, Daruma, Moiwa, Shibuya Sky, PARCO, Ikebukuro, City Hall view. Out: Enoshima/Slam Dunk and Fujiten ski (no day free near them; Niseko is the better ski), Toyota museums (Nagoya off route), Cape Kamui (path closed in winter), Nissan Crossing (easy to add on Feb 1 if time), Budokan/Tokyo Station GBC scenes.

cost.transport: ≈ ¥155,000 per person. Tokyo → Kyoto Times car (Prius, 48 h ¥20,300 + studless ¥6,600 + full cover ¥7,600 + one-way ≈ ¥62,000 + tolls ≈ ¥17,000 + fuel/parking ≈ ¥9,000) ≈ ¥123,000 for two; Hokkaido Times 4WD 5 days incl. one-way ¥5,720, tolls, fuel, parking ≈ ¥95,000 for two (Hokkaido price not checked); JAL Itami → CTS ¥13,030; Skymark CTS → Haneda ¥11,750; airport buses ≈ ¥6,700; trains ≈ ¥13,000.
cost.hotels: ≈ ¥136,000 per person. Super Hotel Shinjuku 4 nights ≈ ¥68,000 for two; Hotel Koryu with 2 meals ≈ ¥36,000; Hotel Keihan Kyoto Grande 3 nights ≈ ¥66,000 (not checked); Hotel 3M 3 nights ≈ ¥50,000; Route Inn Sapporo 3 nights ≈ ¥52,000.
cost.activities: ≈ ¥110,000 per person on average (Pegasis ≈ ¥115,000, Aoki ≈ ¥105,000): Rusutsu drift (Pegasis drives ¥31,000 + shared pro ride ¥17,000 + Aoki rear seat ¥10,000), 3.5 ski days with rental, Aoki's 2 lessons, Suzuka, museums, SHELTER, Shibuya Sky, maid cafés, zoo, Moiwa.
cost.total: ≈ ¥400,000 per person, plus food about ¥5,000 a day (≈ ¥75,000) = ≈ ¥475,000. The one-way Tokyo → Kyoto car is the biggest single cost; it replaces about ¥11,000 per person of trains + bag shipping and makes Suzuka possible.

flights: Pegasis: WestJet round trip Toronto ↔ Narita CA$1,039 (Econo, 1 bag included): Mon Jan 18 09:35 Toronto → Calgary → Narita Tue Jan 19 16:30; back Tue Feb 2 Narita 18:30 → Calgary → Toronto 19:20 same day.

Aoki: Spring Airlines Shanghai Pudong → Narita Tue Jan 19 15:00 → 18:40 (CA$304, 1 bag); home Air China Narita → Pudong Tue Feb 2 15:00 → 17:25 (CA$371; check the bag rule). Option: Air China in 09:40 → 13:40 (CA$376) to arrive before Pegasis.
Osaka → Hokkaido: JAL Itami → New Chitose Tue Jan 26 10:50 → 12:35, ¥13,030 per person, 20 kg bag included (Google Flights, Sep 2026). Cheaper but earlier: Jetstar KIX 09:50 → 11:50 ¥7,510 + bag.
Sapporo → Tokyo: Skymark New Chitose → Haneda Mon Feb 1 10:35 → 12:20, ¥11,750 per person, bag included (Google Flights, Sep 2026).

Pegasis: ask for a paper entry stamp at immigration. Rental car shops sometimes want to see it with the IDP.

places.blurb: A narrow alley of tiny yakitori bars beside the Shinjuku tracks. A good first dinner after a long flight.
tips: Many bars add a seat charge (お通し) of ¥300–500. This is normal.

places.blurb: About 200 tiny bars in 6 narrow lanes, 10 minutes on foot from the hotel. One drink here if you still have energy.

info.label: Hours
info.value: Evenings, many bars open until late

tips: Look for a sign at the door: some bars do not take tourists or charge a cover.

places.blurb: The red-railed stairs from the last scene of Your Name. A 15-minute stop on the way to Akihabara.

info.label: Station

info.label: Pay

places.blurb: The Bocchi the Rock! town: narrow streets of used clothes, records and small live houses.

info.label: Dinner

places.blurb: The real live house behind STARRY in Bocchi the Rock. You buy a ticket and stand inside for a real indie band show.
tips: Ticket pick-up is often at 7-Eleven or FamilyMart. Queue by the number on the ticket. Standing only.

places.ja: カップヌードルミュージアム横浜

tips: My Cup Noodle Factory tickets can sell out: buy a timed ticket on the site.

Ask for studless tyres (スタッドレスタイヤ, ¥2,200 per 24 h outside snow areas) and an ETC card when you book.

places.blurb: Japan's biggest Chinatown. Early dinner of dumplings and buns before the night drive.

info.label: Parking
info.value: Many coin car parks, about ¥400/30 min

places.blurb: The famous JDM car meet spot inside a giant expressway loop. Pegasis drives in himself, no guide.

info.label: Access

tips: Look, do not touch the cars. Ask before you take close-up photos of people.
If police close the PA, the gate is shut: drive on to Umihotaru.

places.blurb: A rest-stop island in the middle of Tokyo Bay. You drive 9.6 km under the sea to get there.

info.label: Toll
info.value: Aqua-Line with ETC about ¥800–1,600 each way (cash ¥3,140)

places.blurb: A small parking area with the Tokyo skyline behind the cars. Tuned cars often stop here late at night.

info.label: Closure risk
info.value: Police sometimes close it when busy

places.ja: アネスト岩田ターンパイク箱根
places.blurb: A 14 km private toll road of long, fast curves up to 1,011 m. It is the classic Japanese car-magazine road.
tips: Ice is most common before 10:00, so the plan starts at about 09:50. With studless tyres this is fine; still drive gently on shaded corners.

places.blurb: The top of the Turnpike: Mt Fuji behind Lake Ashi, and a lounge café for car people.

places.ja: 箱根神社・芦ノ湖（元箱根）
places.blurb: The lake of Evangelion's Tokyo-3. Walk to the red torii that stands in the water, then drive north through Sengokuhara, the centre of the anime city.

info.label: Parking
info.value: Paid car parks at Motohakone port

tips: Play the Eva opening song as you drive into Sengokuhara.

places.blurb: A mountain pass on Route 138 with a famous full view of Mt Fuji over Gotemba.

places.ja: 御殿場プレミアム・アウトレット
places.blurb: About 290 outlet shops with Mt Fuji behind them. Lunch here, and buy cheap ski gloves and thermal wear for Hokkaido.

places.ja: 富士モータースポーツミュージアム
places.blurb: Race cars from about 100 years at the gate of Fuji Speedway: the Mazda 787B, Honda RA272, rally cars and the HKS Supra drift car.
tips: Book online a month ahead for the lower price.

places.blurb: The classic view of Mt Fuji across Lake Kawaguchi. At sunset the snow on Fuji turns pink.

Onsen hotel on the east shore of Lake Kawaguchi, with Japanese-style rooms, a dinner and breakfast buffet, and a manga café (りゅうのす) inside. This is the one 'onsen night' of the trip: the draw is the lake view, the dinner and the manga; the bath is only an extra.

info.label: Price
info.value: About ¥33,000–36,000 for two with dinner and breakfast (Expedia, Sep 2026; check the official site)

tips: Ask for a lake-view room.
You leave at 06:40 on Jan 23: ask the evening before for a breakfast box (朝食の軽食), or buy breakfast at a konbini.

places.blurb: Where Rin camps in Yuru Camp episode 1, and the Fuji view on the old ¥1,000 note. Early morning the lake is calm.

info.label: Entry
info.value: Free for a short look; small parking fee may apply

tips: Bring gloves: it is often −5 °C here at 07:00.

places.ja: 鈴鹿サーキット サーキットチャレンジャー
places.blurb: Home of the Japanese F1 Grand Prix. The Circuit Challenger EV kart runs on the real East Course: through turn 1 and the S-curves, no licence needed.

info.label: Open
info.value: Only Jan 22–25 in your dates (closed Jan 12–21 and 26–29)

tips: The January kart calendar comes out on Dec 1, 2026. Book two karts (one each) around 12:00 as soon as it opens.
Honest check: by train this is about 2 h each way from Kyoto, so you would skip it. It fits only because the car already drives past it.

places.blurb: You return the Tokyo car here, on the south (Hachijo) side of Kyoto Station. The Kintetsu line to Nara leaves from the same side.
tips: Fill the tank near the station before you return the car.

places.ja: ホテル京阪 京都 グランデ
places.blurb: Chain hotel at the Hachijo exit of Kyoto Station, 3 minutes from the car return and the Kintetsu line. One base for 3 nights in Kansai.

info.label: To Itami
info.value: Airport limousine bus from the Hachijo exit, about 55 min

places.blurb: The giant wooden hall of the Great Buddha, with the Nara deer all around the gate.
tips: Deer bow for crackers, but they also push and nip. Hold the crackers up and show empty hands when done.

places.en: Tobihino field (view of the Wakakusa hill fire)
places.ja: 飛火野（若草山焼き 見物）
places.blurb: An open lawn in Nara Park with a clear view of Wakakusa hill. At 18:15, 600 fireworks; at 18:30 the whole grass hill is set on fire.

info.label: Weather
info.value: Cancelled in bad weather, no second date

tips: Be there by 17:30 for a good place. The trains back to Kyoto are full after 19:00: stay 15 minutes longer and go at about 19:30.

places.blurb: Thousands of red torii gates up the mountain. At 07:00 you walk them almost alone.
The Golden Pavilion. If snow fell in the night, the gold temple has a white roof (1–3 mornings a winter).

places.ja: 京都コンサートホール
places.blurb: The building used for the school in Sabbat of the Witch. Outside photos only.
The covered shopping street where the Sabbat heroine takes the giant ramen challenge. Ramen lunch here; you meet again here.

places.ja: スターバックスコーヒー 神戸北野異人館店
places.blurb: A Starbucks inside a 1907 Western house on the Kitano hill. It is the model for cafe Schwarze Katze in Sabbat of the Witch.

info.label: Note
info.value: Renovated, so the inside differs from the game

places.blurb: Kobe's centre. Many teppanyaki shops sell real Kobe beef; an early dinner is cheaper than a late one.
tips: Look for the bronze 'Nojigiku' Kobe beef certificate in the shop.

places.blurb: The big glass mall at Osaka Station used for the date scenes in Sabbat of the Witch.
Osaka's kitchen: grilled scallops, wagyu skewers, tamagoyaki and fruit. Many cooked foods, not only raw fish.

places.ja: 日本橋でんでんタウン・オタロード
places.blurb: Osaka's Akihabara: electronics, figures, games and doujin shops, plus Super Potato for retro games.

places.ja: めいどりーみん 大阪日本橋オタロード店
places.blurb: The Osaka shop of the maid café chain, with stage shows.

places.en: Liberty Walk JDM PARK / LB DRIVE-IN
places.ja: JDM PARK / LB DRIVE-IN（リバティーウォーク泉南）
places.romaji: Ribatī Wōku Jē Dī Emu Pāku
places.blurb: Liberty Walk's own drive-in: wide-body GT-Rs, Lamborghinis and Ferraris, an LB goods shop and an udon shop.
The Glico sign, takoyaki, okonomiyaki and kushikatsu, then small standing bars in Ura-Namba.

info.value: ¥4,000–6,000 per person for many small plates

places.blurb: Osaka's city airport. JAL to New Chitose with a free 20 kg bag.
Sapporo's airport. You pick up the Hokkaido car at the Times shop here (free shuttle), and fly to Tokyo from here on Feb 1.
tips: Buy the last Hokkaido snacks here on Feb 1: Shiroi Koibito, Royce, LeTAO.

places.blurb: Simple hotel in Kutchan town, 15 minutes by car from the Niseko ski areas. Supermarkets and cheap diners nearby.

info.label: Price
info.value: About ¥16,000–17,000 per night for two (Expedia, Sep 2026)

places.blurb: An old family diner: katsu curry, tempura soba, donburi, all about ¥800–1,100.

info.label: Tip
info.value: Last order early; phone first (irregular closed days)

places.ja: ルスツリゾート 雪上ドリフト
places.blurb: A closed snow course on the Rusutsu golf ground. Pegasis drives a Subaru himself with an instructor; both ride with a pro rally driver.

info.label: Pro ride
info.value: Subaru B4 ¥17,000 for 1–2 people; GT-R / GR Yaris ¥27,000

tips: Check in at the Rusutsu Resort Hotel activity desk 20 min early (breath test, then a 15-min shuttle).
Email them first to confirm a 1-year licence + IDP is OK. If not, both take the pro ride instead.

places.ja: ルスツリゾートスキー場
places.blurb: Big ski resort with fewer people than Niseko and good wide beginner runs.

info.label: Half day
info.value: Afternoon ticket (price for 2026-27 not checked, about ¥7,000)

places.ja: ニセコアンヌプリ国際スキー場
places.blurb: The quiet side of Niseko with wide gentle runs for Aoki and deep powder for Pegasis. Cheaper than the all-mountain ticket.
tips: Avoid 'Strawberry Fields': going left leads to steep chutes.

places.ja: ニセコ東急 グラン・ヒラフ
places.blurb: Niseko's biggest ski area, on the side of Mt Niseko Annupuri facing Mt Yotei.

places.ja: ホテルルートイン札幌中央
places.blurb: Business hotel in central Sapporo with a public bath and free breakfast, near Susukino and Tanukikoji.
Sapporo's famous soup curry: spicy broth with big vegetables and chicken. Choose a spice level.

places.ja: めいどりーみん 札幌狸小路店
places.blurb: The Sapporo shop of the maid café, inside the covered Tanukikoji arcade.
King penguins walk in a line through the snow among the visitors. Also polar bears and snow leopards.

places.ja: あさひかわラーメン村
places.blurb: Eight Asahikawa ramen shops under one roof. Try the soy-sauce ramen with a layer of lard on top.

places.ja: 成吉思汗だるま 本店
places.blurb: Grilled lamb on a dome-shaped iron pan, in a small counter shop from 1954.
tips: There is often a queue at 18:00–20:00. Go at 17:00 or after 21:00.

places.blurb: The 1972 Olympic ski hill, 40 minutes from central Sapporo, with a view of the city and the sea.

places.ja: タイムズカー 札幌時計台前店
places.blurb: Car return near the Sapporo Clock Tower, 10 minutes on foot from the hotel. Pin is the Clock Tower.
Ropeway and mini cable car to a summit with one of Japan's best night views of the city.

info.label: Access
info.value: Streetcar to ロープウェイ入口 + free shuttle bus

places.blurb: The meeting place in Girls Band Cry episode 3, at the Shibuya Scramble crossing.
Open-air roof 229 m above Shibuya. Enter before 15:00 for the cheaper ticket and stay to see the sunset and Fuji.
tips: The roof closes in strong wind or rain.

places.blurb: Nintendo's and Pokémon's big Tokyo shops on one floor.

A free view from 202 m, 10 minutes on foot from the hotel. Fuji is clearest on winter mornings.
Shinjuku's big bus terminal on the 4th floor above the JR station. Airport buses to Narita and from Haneda stop here.

notes: Suzuka honestly: it is about 2 h each way by train from Kyoto, so on a train trip you would skip it. If the kart is sold out or it rains hard, skip Suzuka and drive straight to Kyoto (3 h 30).
Both of you drive today in turns of about 1.5 hours. Pegasis takes the expressway, Aoki the city part in Kyoto.

Times has no shop in Nara, so the car goes back in Kyoto; this is also where you sleep.
